 What Mikel Arteta wants from the Newcastle United fans
 An old friend returns to Tyneside
 Friday, 20th November — By Geoffrey Sawyer 
 Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes is now in the red and white of Arsenal 
 MIKEL Arteta is hoping Bruno Guimaraes gets a good reception when he walks back into St James’ Park on Saturday, which might have be seen as a polite way of admitting he might not.
 Arsenal travel to Newcastle at 5.30pm for the Brazilian’s first return since his move from the Magpies in August, a deal reportedly worth £75m.
 Guimaraes, 29, spent four and a half years on Tyneside, captained the club and became the first skipper in seven decades to lift a major domestic trophy for them, after the 2025 Carabao Cup final win over Liverpool.
 Asked whether he would get a good reaction from the home crowd, Arteta said: “I hope so. I think he was one of the main players there, and I think he came to the club at a really important time when they had, obviously, a massive lift in terms of performance and what they have achieved altogether, which was really impressive.”
 Guimaraes called the transfer one of the “toughest decisions” of his life in August, adding: “This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me.”
 He is fit to play after flying back from Singapore with Brazil team-mate Gabriel.
 “Both Gabi and him came back, the same as the other internationals apart from Zubi – so they are in good condition,” Arteta said.
 Martin Zubimendi is out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury picked up on Spain duty.
 Arteta also thinks Guimaraes will help against a Newcastle side now under new head coach Matthias Jaissle.
 “We know the game to expect tomorrow (Saturday), how difficult it is to play against Newcastle, with a new manager, new ideas, obviously new philosophy, and Bruno knows them really well,” the manager said. “So we’re ready for that.”
